haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized at once. Redis is not read or changed, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: 100 per minute in total for a Standard customer. All keys share one customer ID and one budget.
haiku-low.q3: 429 with Retry-After set to seconds left in the minute, and no X-RateLimit headers. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. Denied requests use no budget and are not incremented.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request was already counted, so it uses budget. The gateway returns the backend's 500 response to the client.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway forwards the request anyway (fail open), emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, sends no X-RateLimit headers, and does not retry.
haiku-low.q7: Standard gets 100 requests per minute. Enterprise has no limit yet, because Product has not chosen one.
haiku-low.q8: Redis counter keys rl:<customer ID>:<minute>, shared by all instances. Each key gets a 60-second TTL on its first request and expires on its own.
haiku-low.q9: Each clock minute uses a new counter key, so the budget resets at each new minute. Old keys expire after 60 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: A Redis Lua script, check_and_incr, does the check and increment as one atomic step, so no other command runs between them.
haiku-low.q11: The Lua script returns the seconds left in the current minute, at least 1. Retry-After uses that value; the gateway uses no clock of its own.
haiku-low.q12: No, the gateway does not retry the store. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized at once. Redis is not read or changed, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: 100 requests per minute in total (if Standard plan), because all of a customer's keys share one customer ID and so one budget. (Enterprise has no limit yet.)
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds left in the minute), and no X-RateLimit-* headers. The backend never sees it; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. Denied requests use no budget; the script denies without incrementing.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The request was already counted when allowed, so a backend 500 still uses budget; its response goes back to the client.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: it forwards the request to the backend anyway, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and sends no X-RateLimit-* headers. The count may or may not include the request.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 per minute. Enterprise: no limit yet (Product has not decided one), so Enterprise is not limited in this version.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, shared by all six gateway instances, under the counter key rl:<customer ID>:<minute>. Old counts are removed by the key's 60-second TTL, set when the first request of the minute creates the key, so keys expire on their own.
sonnet.q9: Budget resets when the next clock minute (fixed window) starts: a new counter key is used each minute and the old one expires after its 60-second TTL. No other recovery mechanism is stated.
sonnet.q10: The check and increment are done in one atomic step by the Redis Lua script check_and_incr, so no other Redis command runs in the middle; two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: It is the seconds left in the current minute, returned by the check_and_incr script (based on the Redis server's clock); it is at least 1. The gateway uses no clock of its own.
sonnet.q12: No, the gateway does not retry. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers (no Limit or Remaining, and no Retry-After), just the normal backend response.
